forces.title: Shift to ARPU-Led Growth from Subscriber Additions in Telecom
forces.description: India's wireless market is maturing, leading to a structural shift in telecom sector growth. Subscriber additions are moderating to 3-4% annually, reducing their contribution to overall growth. The focus has decisively moved towards Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) expansion, driven by 2G-to-4G/5G migration, premiumisation, increased smartphone penetration, higher data consumption (26.7 GB/user/month), and improved subscriber quality. This implies revenue growth is no longer solely dependent on periodic tariff hikes, but also organic improvements in monetisation.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: Calibrated Tariff Hike Expected to Drive Next Leg of ARPU Growth
forces.description: With nearly two years passed since the last industry-wide tariff hike (July 2024), CareEdge Ratings expects another calibrated 10-12% tariff hike in the second half of FY27. This hike is anticipated to be a key catalyst for the next phase of ARPU growth, profitability improvement, and returns on significant 5G infrastructure investments. India's mobile ARPU (US$2.5) remains among the lowest globally, despite high data usage, indicating substantial headroom for tariff rationalisation and future increases. This also strengthens the sector's financial profile.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: Completion of Peak 5G Investment Cycle Moderates Capex, Improves FCF
forces.description: The Indian telecom sector is entering a more favorable investment cycle as the aggressive nationwide 5G rollout (FY23-FY25) completes. Operators are shifting from large-scale coverage expansion to selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification. This moderation in capital expenditure is expected to reduce capex intensity from 22% in FY26 to 19% in FY27. This, combined with improved operating leverage from revenue growth, is projected to boost EBITDA margins (55% to 57%) and support stronger free cash flow generation, aiding deleveraging and strengthening credit profiles.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: “Free Music” Culture and Piracy Undermine Paid Streaming Monetization
forces.description: The digital revolution, offering millions of tracks via single apps, has fostered a prevalent 'free music' culture, with piracy and ad-supported freemium models (like YouTube) leading consumers to perceive music as an unpriced utility. This significantly hinders monetization efforts, as only 14 million paid music subscriptions existed in India by December 2025. This non-paid ecosystem negatively impacts creators and copyright owners, creating a paradox where high consumption doesn't translate into willingness to pay, a key challenge for the music industry.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Telecom Bundling Enhances Reach and Trial of Premium Digital Services
forces.description: Bundling digital services, including music streaming, with telecom subscriptions presents a significant opportunity to expand reach and encourage trial of premium offerings. While bundling currently drives usage more than perceived standalone value, it serves as a critical distribution mechanism, especially for services priced below INR100 per month. Increasing bundling with high-reach utility apps, online banking, and sports apps, alongside family-friendly multiple user plans, can help convert fence-sitters and deepen digital penetration across India's vast smartphone user base, ultimately driving future paid subscriptions.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Technology and Telecommunications Sector Shifting from AI Experimentation to Scaled Deployment
forces.description: The technology and telecommunications sector is transitioning from exploratory AI initiatives to widespread, scaled deployment across core operations. Over 90% of organizations are actively deploying AI, cloud, data, and cybersecurity, with AI contributing 21-40% of total digital value. This shift emphasizes moving beyond pilot programs to enterprise-wide implementation and generating consistent ROI across multiple use cases. The sector is focused on transforming technology investments into measurable business outcomes, underscoring a maturity phase where execution quality and the ability to simplify complexity define performance and competitive advantage.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Legacy Systems and Rapid Change Erode Technology Investment ROI
forces.description: A significant challenge for technology and telecommunications organizations is the erosion of returns from technology investments due to legacy systems and processes. 60% of respondents report that legacy infrastructure reduces the effectiveness of their investments, while 61% state that technology plans quickly become outdated due to the rapid pace of change. This indicates that while investment is substantial, execution friction remains widespread, and organizations struggle to consistently convert capital into optimal outcomes. Overcoming these integration complexities and operating model limitations is crucial for maximizing ROI.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Robust Government Investment in Digital Infrastructure and Rural Connectivity
forces.description: The Indian government is significantly boosting the telecom sector through substantial investments in digital infrastructure. The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹73,991 crore (USD 8.37 billion) to the Department of Telecommunications, a 39% increase over FY25-26 estimates. Additionally, approximately USD 17.0 billion (₹1.50 lakh crore) is being deployed through the BharatNet programme to connect 260,000 Gram Panchayats with high-speed broadband. These initiatives aim to strengthen rural connectivity, support nationwide 5G deployment, and lay the foundation for future 6G services, driving long-term growth and digital inclusion across the country.

forces.title: PLI Scheme and Policy Support Foster Indigenous Telecom Innovation
forces.description: The Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for telecom and networking products, allocated Rs. 1,950 crore (US$ 220.7 million) in the Union Budget 2026–27, aims to establish India as a global manufacturing hub for telecom equipment. Complementary policies like the revamped Technology Development and Investment Promotion (TDIP) Scheme (Rs. 203 crore for FY26–FY31) and reduced Telecom Security Testing Laboratory (TSTL) fees promote indigenous innovation, strengthen India's participation in global telecom standards, and support startups, MSMEs, academia, and industry players in developing next-generation telecom technologies.

forces.title: Satellite Communications Sector Set for Robust Growth with Formalizing Regulatory Frameworks
forces.description: India's satellite communications (SATCOM) sector is projected for robust growth, with the market expected to double over the next few years. Union Minister for Communications Mr. Jyotiraditya M. Scindia highlighted the government's proactive approach, noting that three SATCOM licenses have already been issued. Regulatory frameworks and licensing processes are being formalized, creating a more conducive environment for investment and expansion. This supportive policy environment, coupled with increasing demand for satellite-based connectivity, positions the sector for significant development and market expansion.

forces.title: Widespread 5G Migration Reshaping Mobile Subscriber Landscape
forces.description: India's mobile market is undergoing a significant structural shift as users rapidly migrate from 4G to 5G networks. 5G subscriptions reached 430 million by the end of 2025, constituting 35% of total mobile subscriptions, while 4G's dominance is projected to wane. 4G subscriptions are forecast to decline from around 570 million in 2025 to nearly 160 million by 2031, with users transitioning to 5G. This widespread adoption, driven by extensive network rollout across 99.9% of districts, marks a fundamental change in network technology and usage patterns, impacting operator strategies and service offerings.

forces.title: BharatNet and 4G Saturation Projects Boost Rural Telecom Infrastructure
forces.description: Government initiatives like the BharatNet project are significantly expanding broadband connectivity, making 2,17,805 Gram Panchayats service-ready by February 2026. Complementing this, the 4G Saturation Project has commissioned 24,263 mobile towers in remote and rural areas by the same period. These programs are crucial for enhancing last-mile connectivity and upgrading network resilience, thereby driving digital inclusion and supporting the overall growth of fixed-line and mobile telecom services in underserved regions, fostering a more connected India.

forces.title: Tejas Networks Secures Key Backhaul Equipment Deal with Vodafone Idea
forces.description: Tejas Networks, a Bengaluru-based gear maker, has secured a significant three-year deal (2024 to 2027) with Vodafone Idea (Vi). This contract involves supplying backhaul equipment crucial for Vi's 4G and commercial 5G networks. Such deals underscore the ongoing demand for telecom network equipment, driven by operators' continuous investments in upgrading and expanding their network infrastructure to support advanced mobile services. This also strengthens domestic manufacturing capabilities in telecom equipment, aligning with broader policy initiatives for indigenous innovation.

viewpoints.title: India's Telecom Sector Shifting to ARPU-Led Growth with Moderating Capex and Deleveraging
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects India's telecom sector revenue to grow 12-14% in FY27, driven primarily by a 10% rise in Average Revenue Per User (ARPU). This shift reflects market maturity, with subscriber growth moderating and focus moving to monetizing the existing base through 2G-to-4G/5G migration, premiumization, and increased data consumption. The sector is also past its peak 5G investment cycle, leading to moderating capex intensity (19% in FY27 from 22% in FY26) and improving EBITDA margins (57% in FY27 from 55% in FY26). This supports stronger free cash flow and deleveraging, with net debt-to-EBITDA projected to decline from 3.0x to 2.3x.
viewpoints.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

viewpoints.title: Technology and Telecommunications Sector Poised for Sustained Growth with AI-Led Execution
viewpoints.description: KPMG's global report highlights strong confidence within the technology and telecommunications sector, with 95% of leaders expecting revenue growth over the next two years. The sector is characterized by significant, sustained investment in digital technologies, with over 90% actively deploying AI, cloud, data, and cybersecurity. The focus is shifting from adoption to execution and scaling, with AI contributing 21-40% of digital value for most organizations. While legacy systems and rapid change pose challenges, disciplined portfolio management, platform-based strategies, and strong governance are driving competitive advantage.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

viewpoints.title: India's Telecom Sector Positioned for Sustained Growth with Expanding Connectivity and FDI
viewpoints.description: India's telecommunications sector is poised for sustained growth, supported by substantial government investment and robust expansion in subscriber bases. The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated Rs. 73,990 crore (US$ 8.37 billion) to the Department of Telecommunications, emphasizing rural connectivity and infrastructure. India holds the second-largest telecom network and internet subscriber base globally, with total telephone subscribers reaching 1,337.54 million and internet subscribers crossing 1.09 billion by March 2026. High FDI inflows (US$ 40.19 million from April 2000-March 2026) further underscore the sector's attractive investment climate and growth potential.

viewpoints.title: Government Investments and Policy Support Propel Telecom and Satellite Communications Growth
viewpoints.description: India's telecommunications sector is receiving significant governmental backing, including a ₹73,991 crore (USD 8.37 billion) allocation in the Union Budget 2026–27 for the Department of Telecommunications, marking a 39% increase. This emphasizes rural connectivity and digital infrastructure expansion like the BharatNet programme (USD 17.0 billion). India’s satellite communications (SATCOM) sector is also projected for robust growth, with the market expected to double. Furthermore, the PLI scheme for telecom and networking products, along with reduced TSTL fees, fosters indigenous innovation and strengthens India's global telecom standards participation, signaling a positive outlook.

demand_drivers.description: Driven by 2G-to-4G/5G migration, premiumisation, rising smartphone penetration, higher data consumption (26.7 GB/user/month in March 2026), and improved subscriber quality (VLR ratio 93.7% in June 2026).
Moderating to 3-4% per annum as the wireless market approaches maturity and penetration is elevated.

pnl_drivers.description: Expected to improve from 55% in FY26 to 57% in FY27 due to operating leverage from revenue growth and moderating capex intensity.
Expected to moderate to 19% in FY27 from 22% in FY26 as the peak 5G investment cycle completes, shifting to selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification.
Expected to decline from 3.0x in FY26 to 2.3x in FY27 due to stronger free cash flow generation and deleveraging from improved EBITDA and moderated capex.

new_opportunities.description: Significant headroom for further tariff rationalisation given India's low mobile ARPU (US$2.5) despite among the world’s highest mobile data usage (26.7 GB/user/month). A 10-12% tariff hike in H2 FY27 is likely.
Continued premiumisation through higher-value plans and bundled offerings is driving ARPU growth, independent of tariff hikes.
Currently limited direct monetisation of 5G services (unlimited 5G data bundled into existing plans). Future opportunity for differentiated 5G pricing.

market_sizing.methodology: CareEdge Ratings projects industry revenue growth composition and ARPU recovery across operators based on annual reports and TRAI data. Forecasts are based on anticipated tariff hikes, premiumization, 2G/4G/5G migration, smartphone penetration, and data consumption.
market_sizing.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

demand_drivers.description: India is one of the fastest-growing digital music markets globally, driven by over 584 million smartphone users in 2025 and low data charges, with over one billion active mobile broadband connections.

Digital revolution inadvertently fostered a 'free music' culture, with many users relying on ad-supported freemium models, particularly platforms like YouTube, reducing willingness to pay for subscriptions.
India's young audience (65% under 35) is a key driver of digital consumption, including music streaming.
Music discovery is primarily visual-first, driven by reels and short-form video, with users moving to streaming platforms for full tracks after an emotional hook.

pnl_drivers.description: The current music ecosystem is heavily reliant on advertising revenue due to prevalent free models, negatively impacting creators and copyright owners. A shift to a tiered paid ecosystem is needed for sustainable monetization.

new_opportunities.description: Bundling music services with telecom and video OTT platforms can increase reach and trial of premium paid services, especially when combined with high-reach utility apps.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Bundling with telecom and OTT platforms

new_opportunities.description: Seamless jumps from short-form video (reels) to full-track listening can enhance discovery and user engagement, driving consumption on dedicated music platforms.
Encouraging large free music platforms like YouTube to aggressively provide offers for premium subscriptions could convert a significant portion of the ad-driven audience to paid tiers.

market_sizing.methodology: Surveyed over 15,000 smartphone owners by IMI and EY. Analyzes music consumption habits, platform preferences (DSPs vs YouTube), willingness to pay, and reasons for paying/not paying. Discusses factors for unlocking paid music streaming growth.
market_sizing.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

demand_drivers.description: Increasing population drives demand for telecommunication services.
Government focus on rural connectivity and telecom infrastructure expansion (e.g., USOF) drives subscriber growth in underserved areas.
Overall tele-density increased, indicating broad market penetration and continued adoption.

market_sizing.methodology: Total number of telephone subscribers in India (wireless and wireline).

demand_drivers.description: Rapidly expanding connectivity across both urban and rural regions fuels growth in internet subscribers.
Continued emphasis on rural connectivity and telecom infrastructure expansion (e.g., USOF) supports internet subscriber growth.

market_sizing.methodology: Total number of internet subscribers in the country.

demand_drivers.description: Broadband subscriber base grows due to increased digital adoption and user engagement across various online activities.
Accessibility of affordable data plans and smartphones drives broadband penetration.

market_sizing.methodology: Total broadband subscriber base in India.
market_sizing.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Rapid expansion of 5G services across all States and Union Territories (99.9% of districts) drives subscriber adoption.
4G subscriptions are forecast to decline as users migrate to 5G networks, boosting 5G adoption.

market_sizing.methodology: Number of 5G subscriptions in India, accounting for 35% of total mobile subscriptions.

demand_drivers.description: India's position as the largest consumer of mobile data globally drives high average monthly usage.
Widespread availability of affordable data plans and rapid 5G adoption contributes to exponential growth in data consumption.

market_sizing.methodology: Average monthly mobile data usage per smartphone in India.

demand_drivers.description: The wireless segment's overwhelming share (96.4%) in telephone subscriptions reflects widespread mobile adoption and preference over fixed lines.
Significant rural subscriber base (41.5% of total) indicates expanding connectivity beyond urban centers.

market_sizing.methodology: Share of wireless and wireline segments in total telephone subscriptions.

demand_drivers.description: Continued growth in wireless subscriptions driven by expanding mobile and Fixed Wireless Access adoption.
Market leaders like Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel, and Vodafone Idea drive subscriber growth through competitive offerings.

market_sizing.methodology: Total number of wireless (mobile + Fixed Wireless Access) subscribers.

demand_drivers.description: Increasing demand for high-speed internet drives growth in wired broadband connections.
Top five service providers account for 98.61% of the subscriber base, reflecting mature market dynamics and focused expansion.

market_sizing.methodology: Number of wired broadband subscribers in India.

demand_drivers.description: India holds the distinction of being the largest consumer of mobile data globally, driving massive wireless data usage volumes.
Significant contributions from 4G (60.13%) and rapidly growing 5G (39.68%) data usage fuel the overall volume.

market_sizing.methodology: Total volume of wireless data usage in India.

demand_drivers.description: YouTube's position as a preferred ad-based platform for music consumption drives massive streaming volumes.
As a video/content sharing platform, YouTube facilitates music discovery and consumption, especially for ad-driven content.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated number of music streams consumed on YouTube, identified as the top ad-based platform for music consumption.
market_sizing.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

demand_drivers.description: Growth in mobile, broadband, and internet subscribers drives overall telecom revenue.
Exponential growth in wireless data usage contributes significantly to revenue.

market_sizing.methodology: Gross revenue (AGR) of the telecom industry.

demand_drivers.description: Increasing demand for mobile and internet services drives TSP revenues.
Q4 performance can be influenced by seasonal factors and year-end financial activities.

market_sizing.methodology: Cumulative gross revenue of telecom service providers (TSPs) in the December 2025 quarter.

demand_drivers.description: Telecom companies require tower infrastructure for expanding rural networks and improving service quality in urban areas.
Continued deployment of 4G and 5G networks necessitates significant investment in passive infrastructure.

market_sizing.methodology: Expected capital expenditure by independent telecom tower companies to support network expansion and quality improvement.
